rounds.text: Helloji Holidays Ltd currently trades at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E of 31.6x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 16.2x, both of which sit well above their respective sector benchmarks of 23.6x and 11.3x [E6, E11]. This expensive pricing is increasingly difficult to justify given the company’s recent operational deterioration, characterized by a 2% decline in trailing twelve-month sales and a sharp 35% contraction in profit growth [E15, E18]. Furthermore, the company is failing to convert its reported profits into actual cash, evidenced by a negative cash conversion ratio of -1.75x and negative free cash flow of Rs -2.23 Cr in March 2026 [E24, E26]. The efficiency of the business is also under pressure, as debtor days have ballooned from 54.6 to 72.3 days and working capital requirements have nearly doubled from 31.8 to 61.6 days [E43, E44]. Institutional confidence appears to be waning, highlighted by a massive exodus of foreign institutional investors who reduced their holdings from 5.81% to a negligible 0.07% [E31]. Conceded: the company maintains a debt-free balance sheet [E27, E28] and has demonstrated strong historical profit growth over the past three to five years [E16, E17].
